16 An electric kettle is rated as having an input power of 1.50 kW and an efficiency of 65.0%.
The kettle is switched on for 2.00 minutes.
How much energy is transferred to the water in the kettle?
A
0.975 kJ
B
117 kJ
C
180 kJ
D
277 kJ

hints: Notice the input power is $1.50 \text{ kW}$ and the time is 2.00 minutes - convert the time to $120 \text{ s}$ so you can find total input energy with $E = Pt$.
Recall efficiency links useful output to total input by $\text{efficiency} = E_{useful} / E_{input}$, so the energy to the water is only 65.0% of the input energy.
First calculate $1500 \text{ W} \times 120 \text{ s}$ in joules, convert to $\text{kJ}$, then multiply by 0.650 and check which option matches.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: input power $P = 1.50 \text{ kW} = 1500 \text{ W}$, time $t = 2.00 \text{ minutes} = 120 \text{ s}$, and efficiency $= 65.0\% = 0.650$.
Find the total electrical energy supplied using $E_{input} = P t$.
Substitute values with units: $E_{input} = 1500 \text{ W} \times 120 \text{ s} = 180000 \text{ J} = 180 \text{ kJ}$.
Use efficiency to find useful energy to the water: $E_{useful} = \text{efficiency} \times E_{input}$.
Calculate: $E_{useful} = 0.650 \times 180 \text{ kJ} = 117 \text{ kJ}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is $1.50 \times 0.650 = 0.975$ with unit $\text{kJ}$, which multiplies power by efficiency but omits the 2.00 minute heating time.

B.explanation: This is 65.0% of the total input energy $180 \text{ kJ}$, giving $0.650 \times 180 \text{ kJ} = 117 \text{ kJ}$ transferred to the water.

C.explanation: This is the total electrical input energy $P t = 180 \text{ kJ}$, before accounting for the 65.0% efficiency.

D.explanation: This divides the input energy by efficiency, $180 \text{ kJ} / 0.650$, which would give an output larger than the input.
